entries.title: Decoding the loopy physics of hula hooping with high-tech earthquake sensors
entries.summary: Hula hooping may be literal child's play, but as it turns out, the physics behind the gym-class staple is so complicated that scientists have spent decades trying to understand how the hula hoop defies gravity.

entries.title: Identical vesicles, different behaviors: Model reveals how spontaneous asymmetry gives rise to lifelike behavior
entries.summary: In nonreciprocal active matter, agents act differently on each other, seemingly in violation of Newton's third law. This principle can result in various active matter traits, such as self-propulsion, molecular regulation and collective motion.

entries.title: Scientists uncover new way to control magnetism and topology using light in atomically thin materials
entries.summary: Envision a material whose magnetic properties and electronic topology can be toggled by exposure to light, paving the way for future electronic devices that do not rely on traditional electrical switching, which wastes energy by producing heat.

entries.title: Order in a quantum chaotic sea
entries.summary: Nature Physics, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03513-y Experiments with a superconducting quantum processor revealed an island of regular motion within otherwise chaotic quantum many-body dynamics and used feedback to steer the dynamics towards it.

entries.title: Light from Disordered Media
entries.summary: Author(s): Marric Stephens Researchers have proposed that structural disorder can be harnessed to generate coherent, directional light from the passage of a charged particle. [Physics 19, s135] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026

entries.title: When simulations fall short, this spectrometer learns for itself
entries.summary: An NMR spectrometer can reveal molecular structure down to the atomic level, but weak signals limit what it can see. Now, Aarhus University researchers have used AI to let the spectrometer learn the best pulse sequence directly from the sample.

entries.title: Slow-motion electron camera reveals light-driven quantum jumps in graphene
